title: FizzBuzz as a Function
statement:
The classic, with a twist: return the answer as a `std::string` instead of printing it.

## Your function

```
std::string FizzBuzz(int n);
```

For `n >= 1`:

- divisible by both 3 and 5 -> `"FizzBuzz"`
- divisible by 3 only -> `"Fizz"`
- divisible by 5 only -> `"Buzz"`
- otherwise the number itself as text, e.g. `"7"`.

## Watch out

- **Test for 15 (or for both factors) first.** If the `n % 3` branch comes first, `15` answers `"Fizz"` and never reaches the combined case.
- **A number is not a string.** `std::to_string(n)` converts it; returning `n` or `char(n)` will not compile or will give the wrong text.

tests.name: multiples of fifteen
tests.description: Both factors: must be FizzBuzz, not Fizz.
